title: He Was Released at ₹23.75 Crore. RCB Bought Him for ₹7 Crore. Venkatesh Iyer Wants India Back.
excerpt: After a dismal domestic season and a KKR exit, the all-rounder scored 209 runs at a strike rate of 186 in six innings and opened the batting with Virat Kohli in the IPL final. Now he says he still believes he can make it back to the Indian team.
body:
Venkatesh Iyer's IPL 2026 arc reads like a story someone would make up. Released by Kolkata Knight Riders after returning just 142 runs from 11 games on a ₹23.75 crore contract — making him one of the most expensive underperformers in IPL history — he arrived at Royal Challengers Bengaluru for a fraction of the price. RCB bought him for ₹7 crore, called him a backup, and seated him on the bench.

Then Rajat Patidar got injured. Venkatesh walked in, scored a half-century, and won the Player of the Match award. When Jacob Bethell could not find form, he was asked to open with Virat Kohli. He never left the opening slot again.

## 209 Runs, 186 Strike Rate, Six Innings

In six innings, Venkatesh scored 209 runs at a strike rate of 186.60. He scored a 16-ball 32 in the final against Gujarat Titans as RCB lifted back-to-back titles. Every game, he walked out with what Aakash Chopra called "sole intent to take on the opposition bowling unit." It worked almost every time.

Chopra, the former India opener turned commentator, identified Venkatesh as one of the less-celebrated but crucial factors behind RCB's triumph. "When he went to RCB, there was a question as to why he was going," Chopra said on his YouTube channel. "They said he will be useful when required, but is a backup option for now, which was an interesting call."

The interesting call paid off. By allowing Venkatesh to open, RCB could play an extra overseas seamer in Jacob Duffy, which strengthened their bowling attack. The tactical flexibility his batting provided was arguably as important as the runs he scored.

## The Road from KKR to RCB

Venkatesh's fall at KKR was steep. In IPL 2024, the Knight Riders had invested ₹23.75 crore in him — the third-highest price paid in that auction — banking on the left-handed all-rounder who had been instrumental in their earlier campaigns. But the returns never materialised. He was shifted around the batting order, struggled for consistency, and was eventually marked for release.

At RCB, the pressure was different. Dinesh Karthik's mentoring environment and the franchise's patient approach gave him space to rediscover his game. He waited through the league stage for his chance. When it came, he seized it with both hands.

"I still feel I can get back to the Indian team," Venkatesh told reporters after the IPL concluded. He is now playing in the Madhya Pradesh Premier League 2026, looking to stack domestic runs that could put him back in the selectors' conversation.

## What the Selectors Are Watching

India's all-rounder spot has been a revolving door. With the Champions Trophy and the World Test Championship cycle running simultaneously, the team management has been looking for left-handed batting options who can contribute with medium pace. Venkatesh, who bowls left-arm medium, fits that template — at least on paper.

The challenge is consistency. Six good IPL innings do not erase a difficult domestic season. Anil Kumble, the former India coach, had predicted before IPL 2026 that Venkatesh would not make RCB's starting eleven. "I don't think Venkatesh Iyer will be part of the playing XI at the start," Kumble told JioHotstar. He was right — until injuries created the opening.

For NRI cricket fans who watched Venkatesh's explosive IPL run from abroad, his story carries a familiar resonance: the second chance, the unlikely comeback, the refusal to let a setback define the career. Whether the selectors agree remains to be seen. But after what he did in six innings for RCB, ignoring him entirely will be harder than it was in January.

## The Numbers Tell the Story

His IPL 2024 season at KKR yielded 142 runs in 11 matches at a strike rate around 120 on a ₹23.75 crore contract. His IPL 2026 season at RCB produced 209 runs in just 6 innings at 186.60, bought for ₹7 crore. Same player, different environment, dramatically different results. Whether that says more about Venkatesh Iyer or about the systems around him is a question worth asking.
